Compiled successfully (the deprecation note is expected — it's the `new AnnotationUtils()` call testing the documented deprecated constructor).

## Summary

Created two self-contained JUnit 5 test classes based strictly on the javadoc contracts in `api/`:

- **`tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/AnnotationUtilsAgentTest.java`** — covers `equals` (null handling, same/different type & value), `hashCode` (cross-checked against the real JDK proxy's own `hashCode()`, plus dynamic-proxy-based tests that trigger the documented `IllegalStateException`/`RuntimeException` cases), `toString`, `isValidAnnotationMemberType` (all documented valid categories: String, Class, primitives, Annotation, Enum, single-dim arrays; plus invalid cases: wrapper types, arbitrary objects, multi-dim arrays), and the deprecated public constructor.

- **`tests/org/apache/commons/lang3/builder/AbstractReflectionAgentTest.java`** — since the class is abstract with a package-private constructor, defines minimal concrete `AbstractBuilder`/`AbstractReflection` subclasses in the same package to exercise it. Covers `getForceAccessible()`'s system-property parsing (unset/true/TRUE/false/invalid), `AbstractBuilder.asThis()`/`setForceAccessible()` fluent returns, `isForceAccessible()` defaulting behavior, and both `setAccessible` overloads (null handling, forced vs. non-forced on a private field verified via actual `IllegalAccessException`/successful access, and already-accessible public fields). The fixture class with the private field is a sibling top-level class rather than nested, to avoid JDK 11+ nestmate privileges masking the accessibility check.

Skipped the package-private `toRegisterPair`/`isRegistered`/`register`/`unregister` methods and the `null`-type case of `isValidAnnotationMemberType` — their contracts (or the `Pair`/`IDKey` types they depend on) aren't documented anywhere in `api/`, so no expectation could be grounded in the spec.

`./compile.sh` reports `compiled OK`.
